top5.why: He owns the area that produced 15.9% of all major+ episodes, and his 130 major episodes are 6.5 times the next candidate's even after the templated catalogue PRs are set aside. His top work fixed fleet-wide stalls and duplicate rows on the shared loader path (#110610 and #113196, both P=16.0) and stopped billing for jobs that never ran (#114623). He then built a credentials service and integrations SDK that 21 products now use (#124844, #125029), and 106 other authors build on his files. The self-inflicted credential outage (#86546 then #122385) and thin review on half his PRs are real, but they do not close a gap this large.

He repeatedly finds a failure class that hurts many teams and replaces it with one shared mechanism. The ingress transport ended silent webhook data loss across at least eight providers (#100292, #101508), the granian pin restored web analytics dashboard latency (#104208), and the ownership reader unified four products (#103852, P=16.0). He is the most trusted approver in the pool (trust_rank P100), 106 authors build on his files, and his 24 change requests were 95% adopted. His own record is clean after merge (0 reverts, 9 follow-up fixes over 516 mature PRs).

He changed defaults that every user and team inherits. The boot document shrank from 544 KB to 10 KB (#94059), lazy relation reads across 275 team-scoped models were batched (#126463), and CI ratchets keep the gains from regressing (#126768). He also fixed a production OAuth incident (#83929, P=13.0), integration-token data loss (#108163, P=16.0) and six access-control gaps (#102477, P=16.0), and 100 authors build on his files. He makes the top 5 despite the pool's lowest quality_rate (0.934), because none of his 20 major PRs was reverted or follow-up-fixed.

top5.justification: Reference-weight sensitivity is low (R rank 11) because his team-leverage and trust metrics are weak, but every judgment layer placed him in the top 5: both independent decisions ranked him #4, and he beat the strongest alternative (rafaeelaudibert) in both presentation orders of a direct comparison. His case rests on delivery importance: 37 major episodes (P95 among the 20), concentrated in company-wide security hardening (CSP enforcement, CA emergency fix). The reference score under-weights that concentration by design, so the verdict overrides it; the self-repair share of his CSP work is disclosed as a red flag.
top5.why: He is the pool's dedicated security owner, with 37 major episodes (2nd of 20) whose content is privilege escalation, cross-tenant access, SSRF and credential exposure. He unified project-access precedence in the core permission layer (#114423, P=16.0), enforced CSP across signed-in, shared and embedded pages (#106238, #116719), and pinned connect-time hosts for every warehouse source (#95376, #101362). He also removed the compromised eMudhra roots from every runtime PostHog ships within three days (#121580, #122294). The CSP repair tail and his weak review network are the cost, but no other candidate reduced company-wide risk as directly.

He completed a cross-cutting storage migration inside the window. Feature-flag calls moved out of the events table through cutover (#110254), a transparent HogQL rewrite (#124397, P=16.0) and removal of its rollout flag (#126076), with every deletion path updated for compliance (#117395, P=16.0). He also fixed silent CDP event drops and /flags 503s on core pipelines (#121819, #108772). He is the go-to reviewer for feature flags and experiments (12 requesters, 2nd of 20). The four-day correction chain after the HogQL rewrite shows the work was not right first time, but every fix was his own and none needed a revert.

Lead author of PostHog Workflows (rank 1 of 41 authors in that area) who also acted as the de facto security owner of CDP destination secrets this quarter, shipping a coordinated leak-remediation campaign alongside the Broadcasts and Customer.io-migration features.

context_summary.primary: Product: Warehouse sources looks like the centre of gravity (`area[Product: Warehouse sources].prs_share` 18.7%, `major_share` 15.9%, `changelog` 46), but much of that is templated catalogue breadth (C10 alone has about 874 add-source/add-table PRs and the changelog themes read '161 new source tables'); the durable leverage in that area is the shared sync pipeline (loader stall #80285, claim-query incident #110610, CDC correctness #82568) and the new credentials service migrated across 21 products (#124844, #125029). The clearest cross-team priority of the quarter was security and data-trust hardening: Django platform has the highest major-to-volume ratio of any area (`area[Django platform (API/models/auth)].major_share` 10.6% on 4.4% of PRs), and at least eight of the twenty candidates carry security majors (C17 with 37 major episodes, C15 with 13 of 26 majors on OAuth/MCP, C12 with 11 of 26 on CDP secrets, plus C10, C03, C02, C14, C01). Ingestion pipeline & CDP (`area[Ingestion pipeline & CDP (nodejs)].major_share` 8.4%, `changelog` 0) is where invisible but critical reliability work lives (C11 #121819, C20 #97591, C12 #89177, C06 #128013), so changelog counts understate it, while the changelog itself is inflated by repeated 'N new MCP tools' entries that count once per area. The script reports no single point of approval, but effective concentration exists: C05 approves 778 of C10's PRs with no blocking review after 2026-08-04 and about 1,200 of C10's 2,939 PRs have no recorded review, so the company's highest-volume stream has the thinnest independent gate; closed review loops (the developer-experience trio C07/C09/C14 in `community[1]` with purity 0.176, the Workflows trio around C12/C20, the C13/C04 pair) mean first_pass_rate is weak evidence and post-merge quality_rate and follow-up fixes are the more reliable quality signals. The structurally critical positions are foundation code (downstream_authors 106 for C10 and C07, 100 for C03, 95 for C15) and cross-community bridging (`bridge[C15].betweenness` 0.0792, `bridge[C14].betweenness` 0.0776, `bridge[C10].betweenness` 0.0746), though C14's bridging comes from CI approvals rather than substantive review.
context_summary.second: PostHog's highest-leverage work in this window was correctness, security and reliability on shared paths rather than new features: Django platform (API/models/auth) holds 10.6% of major episodes on 4.4% of PRs (area[Django platform (API/models/auth)].major_share) and Ingestion pipeline & CDP (nodejs) holds 8.4% on 3.4% with zero changelog entries (area[Ingestion pipeline & CDP (nodejs)].changelog=0), and that is where C17, C15, C03, C07, C11, C20 and C12 landed their critical work; at least seven candidates (C17, C15, C12, C16, C19, C03, C11) shipped several security-class majors each, which reads as an org-wide security push rather than one team's job. The warehouse-sources numbers mislead (area[Product: Warehouse sources].prs_share=18.7%, changelog=46): 2,939 of the team's 2,969 PRs are C10's, roughly 32% of those are templated add-table or add-source PRs, and nearly all of the area's 172 major episodes belong to C10 (130) and C19 (32), so the area's real weight is the shared sync pipeline's incident and data-correctness fixes (#110610, #113196, #82568) and C10's credentials service, not catalogue breadth. Per-area changelog counts are also inflated because one 'N new MCP tools' entry is counted in every area it touches (changelog[Product: Experiments]=3 consists only of such entries). The agent/AI push (Tasks, Desktop, Signals with changelog[Product: Signals]=21, MCP) is the most visible product priority, but much of it is still flag-gated (Autoresearch, the Today rail port, the hog CLI), so part of C01, C18, C08 and C15's agent work is prospective. Structurally there is no single point of approval (single_points=[]), but review runs in closed loops (the devex trio C07/C09/C14, warehouse C10 with C05 at 778 of 854 reviewed PRs and C19 mostly bot-approved, workflows C20/C12, product-analytics C04/C13), so first_pass_rate is weak evidence; the structural signals that matter are foundation code (downstream_authors: C07 106, C10 106, C03 100, C15 95), real bridging (C15 at betweenness 0.0792 with the security team routing auth reviews to him, unlike C14's 0.0776 built on 94% approvals) and the HogQL owner mariusandra in community 3, who is the effective gate on core-engine changes by C11 and C02. Community 1 (community[1].purity=0.176) is the real platform hub: it mixes developer-experience, security, blitzscale and growth (C07, C03, C17, C15, C09, C14), the people who change defaults every other team inherits.

devil.objection: Weak objection: his lead is partly volume that peers barely verified. About 32% of his 2939 PRs are templated add-source/add-table/GA flips (~874), and about 1200 PRs carry no recorded review. The reviewer behind 778 of them (C05) gave zero blocking reviews after 2026-08-04 and up to 71 approvals a day, so the 0.99 first-pass and 0.98 quality_rate are weakly tested. He also caused a fleet-wide credential outage himself (#86546 -> #122385, about 2h), received 31 peer follow-up fixes (9 major), and as a reviewer he is light: 269 approvals vs 1 changes-requested, reviewer importance_flow 4.8, requested_by 7 (P63). None of this offsets 130 major episodes (next best 37) and 129 major fixes such as #110610 and #113196, so the objection does not overturn him.
devil.replacement_reason: C15 is the highest-R candidate outside the Top 5 (67.7, R rank 3) and is a real cross-team multiplier where C10 is not: 50 authors approved across 25 teams, trust_rank P84, bridge_rank 1, and 13 company-wide auth/security majors deep-read at C=3 (#113014, #127775, #105547 P=13).

The templated share (~32%) and the self-caused credential outage are real and are shown on his card as caveats, but even discounting templated work he leads delivery by a wide margin. Both independent decisions ranked him #1.

devil.objection: His trust_rank #1 and 0.997 first-pass rate come from a closed developer-experience loop, not company-wide validation.
